title: Salt reactions - 123 school
heading: Salt reactions
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.
You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.q: What is a precipitation reaction?
questions.a: Two solutions react with each other and a solid forms

questions.q: What is a precipitate?
questions.a: A solid that forms in a solution and sinks to the bottom

questions.q: How can you predict whether a precipitate forms when you mix two salt solutions?
questions.a: You look in BINAS table 35 to see whether a combination of a positive ion and a negative ion is poorly soluble

questions.q: Is AgCl very soluble or poorly soluble in water? (use BINAS table 35)
Is BaSO<sub>4</sub> very soluble or poorly soluble in water? (use BINAS table 35)
Is NaCl very soluble or poorly soluble in water? (use BINAS table 35)
Which ions always make a salt dissolve well?
questions.a: Na<sup>+</sup>, K<sup>+</sup>, NH<sub>4</sub><sup>+</sup> and NO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>. A salt with one of these ions dissolves well

questions.q: What are spectator ions?
questions.a: Ions that do not take part in the reaction and stay dissolved

questions.q: You mix solutions of lead(II) nitrate (Pb(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub>) and potassium iodide (KI). A precipitate of PbI<sub>2</sub> forms. Which ions are the spectator ions?
Write the reaction equation for the formation of the precipitate lead(II) iodide from ions.
You mix silver nitrate and sodium chloride. What is the reaction equation of the precipitate that forms?
You mix barium chloride (BaCl<sub>2</sub>) and sodium sulfate (Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub>). Which precipitate forms?
Write the full reaction equation for mixing BaCl<sub>2</sub> (aq) and Na<sub>2</sub>SO<sub>4</sub> (aq).
The precipitate barium sulfate consists of ions in a lattice. Do you write that precipitate in a reaction equation with or without charges? Give the formula.
Write the reaction equation for the formation of the precipitate calcium carbonate from ions.
Which ions make water hard?
What does limescale in a kettle consist of?
You add soda (Na<sub>2</sub>CO<sub>3</sub>) to hard water. What happens to the Ca<sup>2+</sup> ions?
questions.a: They form a precipitate of CaCO<sub>3</sub> with CO<sub>3</sub><sup>2−</sup> and are removed from the water

questions.q: How can you remove Pb<sup>2+</sup> ions from waste water?
questions.a: Add a solution that forms a poorly soluble lead salt (a precipitate) and then filter

questions.q: Which reaction equation describes the removal of Fe<sup>3+</sup> ions with limewater (OH<sup>−</sup> ions)?
Why can you not remove nitrate ions (NO<sub>3</sub><sup>−</sup>) from water as a precipitate?
questions.a: Nitrates are very soluble, so a precipitate never forms

questions.q: How do you detect chloride ions in a solution?
questions.a: You add silver nitrate; a white precipitate of AgCl forms

questions.q: How do you detect sulfate ions in a solution?
questions.a: You add barium chloride; a white precipitate of BaSO<sub>4</sub> forms

questions.q: How do you detect carbon dioxide, and which reaction takes place?
questions.a: You pass the gas through limewater: it turns cloudy because of the precipitate CaCO<sub>3</sub>. Ca(OH)<sub>2</sub> (aq) + CO<sub>2</sub> (g) → CaCO<sub>3</sub> (s) + H<sub>2</sub>O (l)

questions.q: Which two solutions do you mix to make the poorly soluble salt silver chloride?
How do you separate the precipitate from the solution?
questions.a: By filtering; the precipitate stays behind as the residue

questions.q: How do you get the dissolved salt (with the spectator ions) back from the filtrate?
You mix solutions of sodium sulfate and potassium nitrate. Does a precipitate form?
questions.a: No, all possible salts dissolve well

questions.q: Write the full reaction equation for mixing Pb(NO<sub>3</sub>)<sub>2</sub> (aq) and KI (aq).
What is the formula of the salt that consists of Ca<sup>2+</sup> and PO<sub>4</sub><sup>3−</sup> ions?
Write the reaction equation for dissolving calcium chloride in water.
Write the reaction equation for dissolving aluminium sulfate (Al<sub>2</sub>(SO<sub>4</sub>)<sub>3</sub>) in water.
Write the reaction equation for dissolving sodium carbonate in water.
How many ions form when one formula unit of CaCl<sub>2</sub> dissolves?
How can you see in a reaction equation that a precipitate forms?
questions.a: The formula of the substance is followed by (s), for example AgCl (s)
